Vultr is an independent general-purpose cloud with a large global footprint and a straightforward developer console, and it has built out a GPU catalogue on top: NVIDIA A100, L40S, A40, GH200, H100, B200 and AMD MI300X, sold as Cloud GPU instances or bare metal. Vultr's published GPU rates verified in late August 2026: A100 PCIe 80GB $2.397/hr, L40S $1.671/hr, A40 $1.712/hr, GH200 $1.99/hr per GPU, and B200 around $8.50/hr per GPU normalised from its 8× bare-metal node. H100 and AMD MI300X are available in larger shapes; many high-end configurations are reserved-contract rather than genuine on-demand.

I tested Vultr over a six-week period in Q2–Q3 2026, running workloads across three regions: New Jersey (ewr), Amsterdam (ams), and Tokyo (nrt). For bare metal, I provisioned an Intel Xeon E-2288G instance and ran Sysbench CPU, FIO disk, and iPerf3 network benchmarks. For GPU instances, I ran NVIDIA A16 and A100 80 GB instances with PyTorch 2.3 training loops on a ResNet-50 CIFAR-10 benchmark and a small 7B parameter LLM fine-tuning task using LoRA. I measured provisioning latency (time from API call to SSH-accessible), hourly billing accuracy against the stated rate card, and autoscaling behavior. I also opened four support tickets at varying urgency levels to measure response times. All pricing was verified against Vultr's published rate card as of August 1, 2026.

...

### GPU Cloud Instances

Vultr offers four GPU instance classes in 2026: NVIDIA A16 ($0.90/hour), NVIDIA L40S ($1.80/hour), NVIDIA A100 80 GB PCIe ($2.50/hour), and NVIDIA H100 SXM ($4.30/hour). All are billed per-hour with no minimum commitment. In my testing, an A100 instance in the NJ region spun up in 4 minutes 18 seconds from API call to GPU-accessible — usable for burst training workloads without committing to reserved instances.

Yes. Vultr offers NVIDIA H100 SXM GPU instances at $4.30/hour as of mid-2026, billed per hour with no minimum commitment or reserved instance requirement. results.title: 10 Best Vultr Alternatives For Enterprises In 2026
results.author: Carolyn Weitz
highlights:
### GPU Capability Depends on the Deployment Model

Vultr’s Cloud GPU portfolio currently includes NVIDIA A16, A40, A100 and L40S configurations. Higher-end accelerators including H100, GH200, B200 and AMD MI355X appear in Vultr’s bare-metal GPU portfolio.

That distinction matters.

An enterprise looking for flexible virtualized H100 or H200 instances may have a different requirement from one prepared to deploy dedicated bare-metal GPU servers.

Capacity also varies by location, so the global GPU catalog should not be treated as proof that a specific accelerator is available in Mumbai, Bangalore or Delhi NCR.

...

### Stopping an Instance Does Not Stop Billing

Vultr bills Cloud Compute, Optimized Cloud Compute and Bare Metal instances hourly up to a 672-hour monthly cap. GPU instances follow a 730-hour model.

A server continues to incur charges while powered off because its resources remain reserved. To stop compute billing, the instance must be destroyed.

That is important for enterprises that regularly suspend development, staging or project environments and assume powered-off resources stop generating compute charges.

...

High-memory H200 access: H200 NVL instances provide 141 GB GPU memory and are available in single- and multi-GPU configurations, including hourly plans for selected configurations.

...

### Pricing

AceCloud publishes India GPU pricing directly in INR.

A 1× H100 HGX instance with 80 GB GPU memory currently starts at ₹180,000 per month. Six-month and annual commitments reduce the effective monthly rate.

A 1× H200 NVL instance with 141 GB GPU memory starts at ₹381.46 per hour or ₹222,775 per month.

Compute, storage, networking, and managed services are priced separately.

...

DigitalOcean’s rapidly expanding GPU portfolio is also concentrated outside India. As of July 2026, its H100, H200, B300 and other GPU Droplets are not listed in BLR1.

That makes DigitalOcean less suitable when an enterprise specifically needs India-hosted AI infrastructure.

### Pricing

CPU Droplets use per-second billing with monthly caps.

GPU capacity is offered through on-demand, 12-month reserved, Spot and contract models depending on accelerator, region and availability. DigitalOcean adjusted selected GPU rates effective August 1, 2026.

results.title: Fireworks is raising on-demand GPU prices up to 30% on September 1 | Beyond the News
highlights:
# Fireworks is raising on-demand GPU prices up to 30% on September 1

Fireworks' current pricing table shows September 1 increases across H100, H200, B200, B300 and GB300 on-demand deployments, with B200 rising from $10 to $13 per GPU-hour. Dedicated training jobs that use the same GPU-hour rates inherit the new economics.

Reviewed and published by Lars Jansen Updated 28 Aug 2026, 10:59 pm NZST 4 min read Copy link

 First published 28 Aug 2026, 10:59 pm NZST 

## Key details

1. The new Fireworks on-demand GPU rates begin September 1, 2026.
2. H100 80GB: $7 → $8 per GPU-hour.
3. H200 141GB: $7 → $8 per GPU-hour.
4. B200 180GB: $10 → $13 per GPU-hour.
5. B300 288GB: $12 → $15 per GPU-hour.
6. GB300 288GB: $18 → $20 per GPU-hour.
7. On-demand deployments are billed per GPU second with no extra startup charges.
8. Region-restricted deployments are priced at a 1.5× premium.
9. Dedicated Training API jobs use the same on-demand GPU-hour pricing.

...

## What changed

Fireworks' current pricing page publishes a two-column transition for its on-demand GPU deployments: prices through August 31 and new rates from September 1, 2026. H100 80GB and H200 141GB increase from $7 to $8 per GPU-hour; B200 180GB rises from $10 to $13; B300 288GB from $12 to $15; and GB300 288GB from $18 to $20. Fireworks bills on-demand deployments per GPU second with no startup charge, and its Dedicated Training API uses the same GPU-hour pricing, so the change affects both dedicated serving and GPU-hour training jobs. Region-restricted deployments continue to carry a 1.5× premium.

## Why it matters

Dedicated GPU economics can dominate the unit cost of high-volume inference, fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning workloads. These increases range from roughly 11% to 30%, large enough to change break-even points between accelerator generations, serverless APIs and competing GPU clouds. The biggest increase is on B200, where a workload consuming 1,000 GPU-hours per month moves from $10,000 to $13,000 before regional premiums or other services. Teams should therefore benchmark completed-task throughput rather than choosing hardware on hourly price or peak specifications alone.

## The September increase varies materially by accelerator

H100 and H200 move from $7 to $8 per hour, about a 14.3% increase. B200 rises 30% from $10 to $13, B300 rises 25% from $12 to $15 and GB300 rises about 11.1% from $18 to $20. The uneven changes can alter the relative cost ranking of GPUs even when performance remains unchanged.

## Training inherits the same GPU-hour table

Fireworks states that Dedicated Training API jobs are priced per GPU hour using the On-Demand Pricing section. Teams running reinforcement fine-tuning or dedicated training should therefore update both serving and training forecasts, not only inference deployment budgets.

## Per-second billing limits idle waste but not rate exposure

On-demand deployments are billed by the second and do not charge extra startup time, which remains useful for bursty workloads. But sustained fleets still absorb the full hourly increase, and a region-restricted deployment costs 1.5 times the listed rate.

## Hourly price is not total inference cost

A more expensive accelerator can still win if it materially improves throughput, latency or batch efficiency. Builders should compare cost per successful request, training run or completed agent task under the exact model, quantization, context and concurrency they use.

...

- The pricing page publishes the dated rate transition but does not explain the commercial rationale for each GPU-specific increase.
- Effective cost varies significantly with model serving efficiency, batching, quantization, context length and utilization.
- Enterprise or negotiated contracts may differ from public on-demand pricing.
